title: Reuse exact child intervals for 70.7x faster warm lever planning
body:
The unchanged selected-word seven-lever planner repeatedly computes the same exact child-cost intervals. This opt-in private session reuses only those immutable Fraction intervals, while executing every original model check, relaxation sum and ceiling bisection. No production entry point or source engine is changed.

On the recorded CPython3.12 fixture, three interleaved repeats have medians **2.494202263s uncached vs0.035259292s warm (70.74x)**. First fill is **1.135x** faster. Python3.14 independently measures76.60x warm /1.148x first fill. These are local planner measurements, not full selected cold-replay speedups. Timings include source/context checks, exact trace recording, serialization/hash and full comparison; process startup and module construction are outside the measured boundary.

Every run preserves the same1771-event,906846-byte complete typed trace and original stdout:1238 child requests,263 model checks,263 relaxation sums and7 ceilings. The initial cache computes1084 intervals and hits154; a repeated fixture hits all1238. The reference retains the engine's existing logarithm caches.

The bounded LRU is private to one authenticated module/precision/runtime context; no persistent cache or past proof-result receipt is loaded. Source bytes, Fraction dependency, precision and callable bindings are checked. Changed contexts clear the cache and reject. Exact integer/Fraction keys prevent float aliasing; new keys and evictions recompute. Profiles are never cached.

Validation:

- Registered CPython3.12 replay and12 controls: argument changes, eviction, type aliasing, keyword fallback, changed profile, invalid models, same-size/same-mtime source changes, precision/function replacement and import-state restoration.
- Five entry-point groups reject source/receipt/coverage corruption, malformed JSON and output overwrite.
- A Git-free read-only15-file execution export passes under CPython3.14 with an identical mathematical receipt and unchanged files; both full timing receipts are retained and source/driver/adapter-bound.
- Canonical main and the two target sources remain unchanged; final overlap refresh has complete pagination and no warnings.

Only `research/exact-child-interval-reuse/` is added. The existing manifest-aware package workflow covers its two declared live inputs. Remaining work is a realistic sequence of different candidate profiles and review of a concrete production caller; the selected frontier and kappa are unchanged.

Credit: Douglas Colkitt with Claude assistance for the unchanged interval engine, lever fixture and model; the retained PR1012 and selected-supplier lineage. New code, measurements and documentation by Gareth Davidson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. No independent human review claimed.
